explanation: In line 11, the filesystem-specific evict_inode function is called, which often deallocates the inode or its private data. Line 14 then attempts to access inode->i_data.nrpages after the potential deallocation.
kobject_put(&q->kobj) at line 3 may free the request_queue if refcount drops to zero. Lines 5 and 10 then access q->elevator and q->queue_flags on freed memory.
iput(inode) at line 11 may trigger inode deallocation. The subsequent access to inode->i_ino in the log at line 12 is a Use-After-Free.
__free_page(page) at line 9 deallocates the page. page_has_private(page) at line 11 then checks flags of the freed page structure.
release_mount_point(mnt) may free mnt. The printk at line 10 then accesses mnt->mnt_devname on freed memory.
kfree(action) at line 6 frees the irqaction. Lines 8 and 11 then access action->thread_fn and action->next on freed memory.
file_free(file) at line 4 frees the file struct. Line 7 then accesses file->f_mode on freed memory.
t->release(kobj) at line 4 is the final destructor. Accessing kobj->parent at line 6 and kobj->name at line 9 are Use-After-Free vulnerabilities.
kfree(bdev) at line 4 frees the block device. The return at line 9 accesses bdev->bd_open_count on freed memory.
__dentry_kill(dentry) at line 6 frees the dentry. Line 9 then accesses dentry->d_sb on freed memory.
kfree(data) at line 4 frees the driver data. The check at line 6 still accesses data->has_pending_io on freed memory since the pointer is non-NULL.
jbd2_journal_put_journal_head(jh) at line 5 may free jh. Line 7 then accesses jh->b_transaction on freed memory.
kmem_cache_free(inode_cachep, inode) at line 6 frees the inode. Lines 10-11 then access inode->i_count and inode->i_state on freed memory.
kfree(sess) at line 5 frees the session. Line 9 then accesses sess->id on freed memory.
kmem_cache_free(bh_cachep, bh) at line 6 frees the buffer head. Lines 8-9 then access bh->b_private and bh->b_end_io on freed memory.
put_super(s) at line 4 often frees the super_block. Line 6 then accesses s->s_root on freed memory.
kfree(part) at line 9 frees the partition struct. Line 11 then sets part->nr_sects = 0 on freed memory.
kfree(pd) at line 6 frees the page data. Line 8 then accesses pd->refcount on freed memory.
fput(f) at line 5 may free the file struct if refcount hits zero. Line 6 then accesses f->f_op on freed memory.
kmem_cache_free(inode_cachep, inode) at line 6 frees the inode. Line 9 then accesses inode->i_sb on freed memory.
